enAudit: G2-292 'Shopping Math: Buying Three Things' — the title AND the instruction ('These baskets hold three things. Add all three prices to find each total.') are false for one card in three. The config is kinds:['total3','total','total3'], so card 2 is a plain two-item total; the fruits render shows mango + kiwi only. Either drop the middle 'total' or reword to 'up to three things'.

G2-295 'Shopping Math: How Much More?' — the same class. kinds:['diff','total','diff'], so card 2 asks for a total, not a difference, while the instruction promises 'Compare two prices and work out the difference between them.' The toys render confirms: card 2 reads 'Emma wants [slide] and [rocket]. How much is that altogether?'

G2-294 'Is There Enough Money?' — the instruction 'Count the coins, then compare them with the price.' describes a control the page does not have. There are NO coins on this face: every card states the amount in numerals ('Anna has 45 c'). G2-293 is the face that actually draws coin discs. Suggest 'Read how much money there is, then compare it with the price.'

G1-263 'ABC Order: Four Words' — the title names an attribute it SHARES with its sibling G1-262: both are base difficulty[1], i.e. four cards. The real difference is the writing lines (G1-262 sets rulings:false, G1-263 keeps them), and that distinguisher is unnamed, so the two faces compete on the same promise. Suggest 'ABC Order: Number Them, Then Write Them'.

G1-282 'Unscramble the Sentence: With Clues' — the instruction says 'The capital letter and the full stop show you where the sentence starts and ends', but the frame set includes questions and the fruits render's first card ends in a question mark ('Is this your pomegranate?'). 'Full stop' is wrong there; use 'end mark', which is what G2-281's own legend chip already calls it.

G2-281 — one page, two names for one thing: the legend chip reads 'End mark' while the title ('Capital and Full Stop') and instruction ('a capital letter and a full stop') say full stop. Pick one term across the capitals-punctuation family.

data/b2/sentences.js frame s2 '{name} feeds the {noun}.' has NO animacy restriction and is applied to inanimate themes. G1-283 card 4 ships the chips feeds / tom / skateboard / the — no order of those words means anything, yet the instruction promises 'the only order that works'. s2 carries uses:['unscramble','fix'], so it can also reach the capitals-punctuation faces G2-281/282. Gate s2 (and any other animate-object frame) to animal/person themes.

vocab key 'crane' is the BIRD in German (image-vocabulary.js de: Kranich / Kraniche) but the artwork at 'image library/vehicles/crane.png' is the construction machine, and the vehicles theme is exactly what these faces ship. It reaches G2-287 (word chip 'crane' beside car, bulldozer, airplane, motorcycle), G2-294 (a shelf item with a price tag) and G3-376 ('Ben lines up 30 cranes in 6 equal rows'). German pages will print 'Kranich' among bulldozers. MEMORY.md records this split for es/no/da/sv/fi — de is affected too and is not on that list; the vehicles sense needs its own key (de 'Kran').

G2-298 'Days of the Week' — the render draws two calendar stickers, but this face's question set is ['dayOfDate','countWeekday','firstDay','lastDay'] with no stickerDate, so no question refers to them. They are decorative dead elements here, unlike every other face in the calendar family. Either set stickers:0 or keep one sticker question.

G1-271 'Doubles and Halves to 20' — 'There are no pictures this time' is true of the GIVEN pictures, but difficulty[3] sets numeric:true, which swaps the picture panel for an empty dotPanel on every card, and nothing on the page tells the child what that box is for. Name it ('draw the dots yourself') or remove it.
K-296 'Dot-to-Dot: Count On from 11' — does not state its range while both siblings do (K-294 '1 to 10', K-295 'Teen Numbers'). The page runs 11 to 30. Suggest 'Dot-to-Dot: 11 to 30'.

G1-281 'Where on the Number Line? 0 to 120' — 120 is never printed on the line: with tick:10 and label:5 the printed labels stop at 100. The title names a number the page does not show. Either label the endpoint or retitle.

Shop frames on the animals theme (G2-289, G2-293) put wild animals on a shop shelf with price tags — 'Emma puts [tiger] and [raccoon] in the basket', 'Mia pays for [fish]'. Mechanically fine, but it reads as buying wild animals. Consider excluding wild-animal themes from the shopping frame, as the sellable-item filter already excludes some nouns.

SUSPECTED, not confirmed — G2-300 (fruits) labels one word-bank picture 'cranberry' while the artwork reads as a small red apple with a leaf, and 'plum' as a dark red round fruit. Worth checking 'image library/fruits/' against image-vocabulary.js; flagged as a check, not a defect.

FIVE of the thirteen new faces are the SHIPPED BASE FACE AGAIN. K-312, G1-284, G1-290, G2-309 and G3-377 each spread `base.difficulty[2]` with an EMPTY override, and waves/wave-b2-de.json ships `difficulties:[2]` for every base type — so their resolved config is byte-identical to K-284, G1-245, G1-244, G2-278 and G3-370 respectively (measured by comparing the resolved difficulty[2] objects; the other 75 faces in ROWS are clean). Only the theme and the seed differ. They are second SEO surfaces for a page that already exists, and the English copy invents a distinction the render does not carry: K-312 'Trace Words of Middle Length' vs the base's bare 'Trace and Write the Words', G1-284 'Six Words' vs a base that also shows six, G3-377 'Multiply and Share' vs a base that is already mul+share. Either give each of the five a real config override or drop them from the wave.

G2-306 'Find both capitals, not just the first' is falsifiable twice over. (a) The `fix`+simple frame pool contains a TWO-NAME frame — en '{name} draws two {noun} for {name}.', de '{name} malt {noun} fuer {name}.' — and with needCaps:3 over lanes:3 the selector must pick three name-bearing frames out of six (en) / eight (de) candidates, so that frame can land and the page then wants THREE capitals. (b) lib/sentence-bank.js `corrupt()` lowercases the WHOLE sentence, so in German every Nomen loses its capital too and the child restores four or five per line, never 'both'. Suggest 'Every sentence names somebody, so more than the first word needs a capital.'

G1-286 'Count the bigger groups, double them, and halve them.' describes an operation no card asks for. cards:4 renders two `data-lcs-op=double` cards and two `data-lcs-op=half` cards, each carrying its own pill; no card asks for both. On a doubles card the mirror group is ALREADY drawn and the printed strip is `n + n = box`, so the group the child counts is n (5-10), not 'the bigger' one. Suggest 'Some cards ask you to double a group of pictures, others to halve one — now up to 20.'

G1-290 'One Box for Each Letter' is false for any hyphenated or apostrophised noun. `letterBoxes({ n: [...word.replace(/[ ]/g,'')].length })` strips spaces only, while the G1-244 pool filter admits `'`, `’` and `-`, so de 'U-Boot' would draw six boxes for five letters. de G1-290 ships on `fruits`, which has no such noun, so this face is safe as configured — but the same d2 config reaches the base G1-244 and the vehicles/animals themes (de 'U-Boot', 'U-Bahn', 'Orang-Utan'). Strip the separators in the box count as well, or the title stops being true.

PROCESS, not English: out/b2var-faces.json is STALE — 64 rows against 80 in tools/gen-b2var-specs.js ROWS — and out/b2var-sweep holds 64 PNGs, none of them for these thirteen ids. The file's own docblock says 'RE-RUN THIS AFTER EVERY CHANGE TO THE SPECS OR THE WAVES' and warns that a panel briefed from a stale table is briefed from prose, which is the failure it exists to prevent. This panel worked from the spec modules and each base's build() instead; re-run gen-b2var-faces.js and the sweep before the next slice.

K-312 'Longer words than the first page' names no page. Its siblings are K-289 (<=5 letters) and K-291 (8-12), so 'the first page' could be either, and per the first finding K-312 is itself the base face. Name the comparison or drop it.

CHECKED AND CLEAN, recorded so nobody re-files it: K-308, G1-285 and G2-304 inherit `window:10` from K-285.difficulty[1], so they number only TEN of the twenty dots and pre-print the rest in light ink. All four dot-to-dot ranges in the English are therefore correct (10..1, 2..20, 5..50, and G1-294's full 20..1 with window:null). K-285.verify() also does NOT fail on them: dot-figure stamps `data-lcs-count = labelled`, not the requested count, and the already-shipped K-294/K-295 carry the same window:10 config.

K-309 ABC dot-to-dot: the EN instruction says "in alphabet order" but never says the run is a-t (20 of 26 letters), so a child who expects to reach z reads the page as unfinished. The German names the range.

K-313 vs K-316 read almost identically in EN ("the word for many is given" / "read the word for many") while the pages differ in the one thing that matters: K-313 prints a DASHED singular to trace, K-316 prints nothing at all. Neither EN instruction mentions the model.

G1-297 "Bigger groups to halve, starting from twenty" is wrong: hMin/hMax are 5-10, so the printed groups run 10 to 20 and only the largest is 20. Nothing starts at twenty. (G1-296 says "all the way to twenty", which is correct.)

G1-300 "Sort each word into the right bin" is generic - it names nothing that separates this face from G1-293 or from the three shipped G2 word-classes faces. Its real distinguishing features are TWO bins and NO pictures.

G2-311 "Split them and mark each one" omits the only thing that separates it from G2-307: ends is [".","?"] with needQ 1, so one of the two run-together sentences is a QUESTION and the child must choose the mark. G2-307 is full stops only.

G2-307 and G2-311 titles are near-twins ("Fix the Sentence: Where Does It End?" / "Where Does It End?"). They pass the byte-identity gate but read as the same page; the second should carry the end-mark choice.

G2-312 "Use the calendar to work out each date" is generic, and its question set is G2-297 minus countWeekday - so the genuinely new thing (every question is a date or an interval, none is a tally of weekdays) is stated nowhere.

G2-314 is the only dot-to-dot in the batch that inherits window:10 without saying so. K-308, G1-285 and G2-304 all end "the rest of the outline is already drawn"; G2-314 says only "Join the dots counting in tens to 100", so the pre-printed remainder reads as a printing fault.
G1-287 "Say it, then write the answer" describes a two-step flow the card does not have - there is nothing on the card to say aloud, only a group of pictures and an equation with one answer box.
G1-286 "Count the bigger groups, double them, and halve them" reads as three operations on one group. Each card does exactly one: two cards double, two halve.

G1-303 "the first letter is already there" is ambiguous next to a row of empty letter boxes: the starter is printed on the writing RULING, not inside the first box, so a child looks for a letter in box one.
G1-293 "Two bins this time" is a comparative against a sibling the child cannot see. On a standalone printable there is no "last time".
G2-308 omits that the blank code boxes are GROUPED BY COLOUR - the child writes each code in its own colour group, which is the whole reason the page carries more than one list.
